name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Three dairy-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Washington's three H5N1 cases are all linked to dairy cows; Oregon reports first infected herd; no human-to-human spread
state: Yakima County, Washington, has reported three human H5N1 cases this month, one fatal, all with occupational exposure to dairy cows; Oregon confirmed its first infected dairy herd (CIDRAP, 12 Nov). CDC's update of 13 Nov reports no indicators of unusual influenza activity in people (CDC). With no investigation into human-to-human spread found by 17 Nov, these remain animal-to-human cases and the level stays Normal.
for_you: Risk to the general public remains low, according to CDC; people who work with dairy cattle or poultry face higher exposure. In the UK, Defra and UKHSA publish guidance on avoiding and reporting sick or dead birds.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only: three dairy-linked cases in Washington, no human spread = Normal

sources.title: Oregon logs its first H5N1 case in cows; farmer's union says human avian flu cases underreported in Washington

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.
